feedback:
Approved, because only one run remains this iteration. A revise decision would need a review and a revision before the race, so the iteration would end unscored.

The candidate is a single-parameter change from the last race (iteration 1: ki 0.4, kp 2.5, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4). It raises ki to 1.0 and keeps geometry, kp, kd, base_speed and line_loss the same. Iteration 1 showed progress moving modestly (oval 0.105 to 0.168, s-bend 0.148 to 0.172, slalom 0.105 to 0.113), with max_error still at the 0.06 off-track limit on every track and rms_error down slightly. That is consistent with a steady offset that the integral only partly removes, so a larger ki is the sensible next test. The stated 2.0 clamp on the integral limits windup. Steering_oscillation stayed below 0.15 on all tracks, so kp and kd have no jitter evidence against them.

No outcome is stated for this candidate. The main risks, judged from the earlier races and the candidate's contents alone, are slow overshoot from the larger ki and base_speed 1.4, which is below the roughly 1.5 m/s average the contract implies for a sub-3 s finish. Read the next race per track: progress, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and completion_time. If progress stays near 0.17 with a constant-sign error, the offset is not the main cause, so look at sensor placement or line-loss behaviour rather than gains. If steering_oscillation rises with a sign-alternating error, reduce ki or kp before touching kd.
requested_changes: If progress is still near 0.17 with a constant-sign error and max_error near 0.06, keep ki at about 1.0 and test sensor placement (for example wider x spacing of the outer sensors) or line_loss as last_direction versus search_left, since the offset hypothesis would then be only partly right.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.15 with a sign-alternating error, reduce ki toward 0.7 and keep kp at 2.5, because the integral is then overshooting.

If any run finishes, read completion_time: if it is at or above about 2.8 s, raise base_speed from 1.4 toward 1.5 to 1.6, since 1.4 is slower than the roughly 1.5 m/s the contract requires for a sub-3 s finish.
